items.description: Homepage presents multiple identifiable intangible-cultural-heritage projects.
items.action: Open the homepage and inspect every visible project list.
items.expected: Multiple project entries are shown, and each entry has enough identifying content to distinguish it from the others.

items.description: Project lists can be filtered.
items.action: Select an available filter whose matching and non-matching projects are known.
items.expected: Only projects satisfying the selected filter remain in the result set.

items.description: Project lists can be sorted.
items.action: Choose an available sort criterion and direction.
items.expected: All displayed projects are ordered according to the selected criterion and direction.

items.description: Selecting a project opens its panoramic scene.
items.action: Click a project in a homepage list.
items.expected: A rotatable 360-degree scene associated with the selected project opens.

items.description: Dragging rotates the panorama.
items.action: Drag horizontally and vertically within a loaded panoramic scene.
items.expected: The viewing direction changes continuously in the corresponding directions.

items.description: Users can zoom the panoramic scene in and out.
items.action: Apply the provided zoom-in input and then the zoom-out input.
items.expected: The scene magnification increases and then decreases without leaving the panorama.

items.description: Perspective and hotspot anchoring continue updating while zoomed.
items.action: Zoom the scene and, while zoom input is active, rotate across one or more visible hotspots.
items.expected: Perspective updates continue without pausing, and each hotspot remains attached to its intended scene location.

items.description: A panorama hotspot opens an information overlay.
items.action: Click a loaded hotspot.
items.expected: An information overlay opens for the hotspot without navigating away from the scene.

items.description: Hotspot overlays contain complete, project-specific summary information.
items.action: Open an overlay and compare it with the selected hotspot and project.
items.expected: The overlay identifies the same project and displays its title, at least one image, origin region, brief description, and a View Details link.

items.description: Different hotspots resolve to their corresponding projects.
items.action: Open two different hotspots in turn.
items.expected: Each overlay shows content corresponding to the hotspot clicked rather than stale content from the other hotspot.

items.description: View Details opens the selected project's dedicated page.
items.action: Open a hotspot overlay and activate View Details.
items.expected: A dedicated detail page for that same project is displayed.

items.description: The detail page contains the full project presentation.
items.action: Inspect a project's detail page.
items.expected: The page shows the correct project identity, a full introduction, and multiple project images.

items.description: Project images can be browsed on the detail page.
items.action: Use the image-browsing controls to move between available images.
items.expected: The displayed image changes to the requested image and remains associated with the current project.

items.description: Returning from details restores the panorama state.
items.action: Rotate and zoom a panorama, open a hotspot and its detail page, then return using the site's or browser's back action.
items.expected: The same scene returns with the prior orientation, zoom level, and corresponding hotspot/overlay state restored.

items.description: Homepage list controls retain their state across project navigation.
items.action: Apply a filter and sort, enter a project scene and detail page, then return to the homepage.
items.expected: The selected filter, sort setting, and resulting project list are preserved.

items.description: Closing an overlay does not reset the manipulated panorama.
items.action: Rotate and zoom the scene, open a hotspot overlay, and close it.
items.expected: The overlay closes while the current panorama orientation and zoom remain unchanged.

items.description: Slow panorama loading produces a visible status prompt.
items.action: Throttle the panorama resource so loading remains incomplete for a noticeable interval.
items.expected: A prompt communicates that the panorama is still loading and disappears after successful loading.

items.description: Unavailable hotspot data produces an explicit prompt.
items.action: Load a panorama while preventing its hotspot or anchor data from loading.
items.expected: The page displays a prompt that the anchor points are not loaded or unavailable instead of showing misleading active hotspots.

items.description: Failed detail-page images produce visible failure feedback.
items.action: Prevent one detail-page image resource from loading.
items.expected: A clear image-load failure prompt or fallback appears while the rest of the detail page remains usable.

items.description: The page presents an identifiable library of technical articles.
items.action: Open the documentation library.
items.expected: One or more distinct technical articles are listed with identifiable titles.

items.description: All three article layout controls are clearly labeled.
items.action: Open an article and inspect its view controls.
items.expected: Separate, understandable controls for Overview, Standard, and Detailed modes are visible.

items.description: Overview mode can be selected.
items.action: Activate the Overview control for an article.
items.expected: The article switches to Overview mode and that control is visibly active.

items.description: Overview mode shows the article title and key points.
items.action: View an article in Overview mode.
items.expected: The correct article title and a concise set of its key points are displayed.

items.description: Standard mode can be selected.
items.action: Activate the Standard control for the same article.
items.expected: The article switches to Standard mode and that control is visibly active.

items.description: Standard mode renders full content with basic formatting.
items.action: Inspect an article in Standard mode.
items.expected: The article's full standard content is present and basic structure such as paragraphs, headings, or lists is rendered legibly.

items.description: Detailed mode can be selected.
items.action: Activate the Detailed control for the same article.
items.expected: The article switches to Detailed mode and that control is visibly active.

items.description: Detailed mode includes expanded material.
items.action: Inspect an article in Detailed mode.
items.expected: The full article is shown with additional material including references and code examples.

items.description: Mode changes do not switch or mix article identity.
items.action: Switch one article through Overview, Standard, and Detailed modes.
items.expected: Every mode continues to show content belonging to the originally selected article.

items.description: Mode switching updates content without requiring article reselection.
items.action: Switch directly from Overview to Detailed and then to Standard.
items.expected: Each requested layout appears immediately for the open article without returning to the library.

items.description: The preferred view persists across future visits.
items.action: Select a non-default layout as the preferred view, leave or reload the page, and open an article again.
items.expected: The newly opened article initially uses the saved preferred layout.

items.description: A newly chosen preference replaces the previous saved default.
items.action: After verifying one saved mode, choose a different mode, leave the page, and revisit an article.
items.expected: The latest chosen preferred mode is used instead of the earlier preference.

items.description: Search finds decisions by decision name.
items.action: Enter a distinctive keyword from a known decision name and submit the search.
items.expected: The matching decision appears in the results.

items.description: Search finds decisions by outcome text.
items.action: Enter a distinctive keyword appearing in a known outcome and submit the search.
items.expected: The decision with that outcome appears in the results.

items.description: Search finds decisions by condition text.
items.action: Enter a distinctive keyword appearing in a known condition and submit the search.
items.expected: The decision containing that condition appears in the results.

items.description: Search results show names and outcome summaries.
items.action: Run a query that returns one or more decisions.
items.expected: Every result displays a decision name and a readable summary of its outcome.

items.description: Multiple filter dimensions can be combined.
items.action: Apply values in at least two available filter dimensions to a known result set.
items.expected: Every remaining result satisfies all selected filter values.

items.description: Changing or clearing filters refreshes results correctly.
items.action: Apply a filter, change its value, and then clear it.
items.expected: The result set updates for each value and returns to the unfiltered query results when cleared.

items.description: A zero-match search has an explicit empty state.
items.action: Search for a string that matches no decision.
items.expected: The page reports that no decisions match and does not display stale prior results.

items.description: Blank searches are handled without creating a misleading query.
items.action: Submit a search containing no keyword and no selected filters.
items.expected: The page either requests search criteria or deliberately shows the full collection, with no error or false match claim.

items.description: A result opens its full decision details.
items.action: Click a decision in the result list.
items.expected: A detail view opens for the selected decision.

items.description: Decision details include conditions and final results.
items.action: Inspect the detail view of a search result.
items.expected: The selected decision's conditions and final result are both displayed in full.

items.description: Result summaries and detail records remain consistent.
items.action: Compare a result's name and outcome summary with the opened detail view.
items.expected: The detail view identifies the same decision and does not contradict the result summary.

items.description: Returning from a detail preserves the active search.
items.action: Run a keyword search with multiple filters, open a result, and return.
items.expected: The keyword, selected filters, and matching result list are restored.

items.description: Submitted searches are recorded in search history.
items.action: Submit a distinctive search query and open the history area.
items.expected: The submitted query appears in the search history.

items.description: A history entry can be used to repeat a search.
items.action: Change the current search, then activate a previous history entry.
items.expected: The recorded search criteria are restored and their results are shown.

items.description: A decision can be bookmarked.
items.action: Bookmark a decision from an available result or detail view and open bookmark management.
items.expected: The selected decision appears once in the bookmarked-decision list.

items.description: Repeated bookmarking does not create duplicate entries.
items.action: Attempt to bookmark the same decision more than once.
items.expected: Bookmark management contains only one entry for that decision.

items.description: Bookmarks can be removed through bookmark management.
items.action: Remove a saved decision from the bookmark-management view.
items.expected: The decision is no longer listed as bookmarked and is shown as unsaved elsewhere.

items.description: Batch import supports Excel, CSV, and PDF inputs.
items.action: Import valid sample files in each advertised Excel, CSV, and PDF format, with each file containing multiple identifiable decisions.
items.expected: Every supported file is accepted and all valid contained decisions become available without silently dropping records.

items.description: Invalid imports produce actionable feedback.
items.action: Attempt to import a malformed or unsupported file.
items.expected: The import is rejected with a clear failure message, and existing decision data remains available.

items.description: Batch export produces complete Excel, CSV, and PDF outputs.
items.action: Select multiple identifiable decisions and export them once in each advertised format.
items.expected: Each export completes in the chosen format and contains every selected decision with recognizable decision, condition, and outcome data.

items.description: Keyword search returns matching adoptable pets.
items.action: Search using a distinctive term associated with a known pet.
items.expected: The matching pet appears and unrelated pets are excluded when they do not match.

items.description: Search results clearly identify pets and their shelters.
items.action: Run a broad search that returns pets from multiple shelters.
items.expected: Each result is distinguishable and identifies its source shelter; the result set can represent more than one shelter.

items.description: Species filtering works.
items.action: Select a species filter.
items.expected: Every displayed pet belongs to the selected species.

items.description: Age-range filtering works.
items.action: Select an age range with known matching and non-matching pets.
items.expected: Every displayed pet falls within the selected age range.

items.description: Size filtering works.
items.action: Select one available size value.
items.expected: Every displayed pet has the selected size classification.

items.description: Good-with-kids filtering works.
items.action: Enable the good-with-kids filter.
items.expected: Every displayed pet is identified as suitable with children.

items.description: Good-with-other-pets filtering works.
items.action: Enable the good-with-other-pets filter.
items.expected: Every displayed pet is identified as suitable with other pets.

items.description: Multiple pet filters use combined criteria.
items.action: Apply species, age, size, and compatibility filters together.
items.expected: Every remaining result satisfies all active criteria.

items.description: Clearing filters restores the broader result set.
items.action: Apply several filters and then use the available clear or reset action.
items.expected: All filter selections clear and the unfiltered search result set returns.

items.description: No matching pets produces a clear empty state.
items.action: Choose a valid combination known to have no matches.
items.expected: A no-results message is shown and stale pet cards are absent.

items.description: Results can be sorted by relevance.
items.action: Choose Relevance from the sort controls.
items.expected: Relevance is shown as the active sort and the matching list is rendered in that ordering.

items.description: Results can be sorted by time listed.
items.action: Choose Time Listed and an available direction.
items.expected: Pets are ordered chronologically by their listing times in the indicated direction.

items.description: A pet result opens the corresponding profile.
items.action: Click a pet in the matching list.
items.expected: A detailed profile for that same pet opens.

items.description: Pet profiles include photos and a description.
items.action: Inspect an opened pet profile.
items.expected: The profile displays the selected pet's identity, one or more photos, and a descriptive adoption profile.

items.description: A pet can be added to favorites.
items.action: Save a pet as a favorite and open the favorites list.
items.expected: The selected pet appears once in the favorites list.

items.description: A favorite can be removed.
items.action: Remove a saved pet from the favorites list.
items.expected: The pet disappears from favorites and its profile or result card reflects the unsaved state.

items.description: Favorites survive ordinary in-site navigation.
items.action: Favorite a pet, browse another result or profile, and return to favorites.
items.expected: The originally saved pet remains in the favorites list.

items.description: Required inquiry data is validated.
items.action: Open the inquiry form on a pet profile and submit it with required information omitted or invalid.
items.expected: The inquiry is not sent and the form identifies the fields that require correction.

items.description: A valid adoption inquiry can be submitted from a pet profile.
items.action: Complete the inquiry form with valid required information and submit it.
items.expected: The form confirms successful submission for the pet whose profile is open and does not report a duplicate send from one submission.

items.description: An ingredient with a quantity and expiration date can be added.
items.action: Add a named pantry ingredient with a valid quantity and expiration date.
items.expected: The pantry displays the ingredient with the entered quantity and expiration date.

items.description: Expiration dates are optional.
items.action: Add a named ingredient with a valid quantity but leave expiration blank.
items.expected: The ingredient is added and is clearly represented without an expiration date.

items.description: Invalid pantry entries are rejected.
items.action: Attempt to add an unnamed ingredient or an ingredient with a zero, negative, or otherwise invalid quantity.
items.expected: The invalid entry is not added and corrective validation feedback is shown.

items.description: Existing pantry entries can be edited.
items.action: Change an ingredient's quantity and expiration date and save the edit.
items.expected: The pantry shows the updated values without creating a duplicate ingredient entry.

items.description: Pantry ingredients can be removed.
items.action: Remove an existing ingredient.
items.expected: The ingredient no longer appears in the pantry or contributes to a newly generated plan.

items.description: A multi-day meal plan can be generated.
items.action: Populate the pantry, choose a plan duration of multiple days, and generate a plan.
items.expected: A plan is produced for every requested day, with one or more identifiable recipes assigned per day.

items.description: Every planned recipe shows exact ingredient usage.
items.action: Inspect each recipe in a generated plan.
items.expected: Each required ingredient has a numeric amount and unit showing exactly how much the recipe will use.

items.description: Ingredient allocation is reconciled with pantry stock.
items.action: Generate a plan containing recipes whose total needs are greater than at least one pantry quantity.
items.expected: The plan does not imply that more pantry stock is available than entered; any deficit is represented as a missing grocery amount.

items.description: Near-expiration food is prioritized.
items.action: Add compatible ingredients with different expiration dates, including one expiring soon, and generate a plan.
items.expected: When feasible, the sooner-expiring ingredient is scheduled earlier or used preferentially over equivalent later-expiring stock.

items.description: The vegetarian preference affects generated meals.
items.action: Enable Vegetarian and generate a plan.
items.expected: Every generated meal conforms to the vegetarian preference.

items.description: The high-protein preference affects generated meals.
items.action: Enable High Protein and generate a plan.
items.expected: The generated meals conform to the page's stated high-protein criterion.

items.description: The budget-friendly preference affects generated meals.
items.action: Enable Budget Friendly and generate a plan.
items.expected: The generated meals conform to the page's stated budget-friendly criterion.

items.description: Compatible preferences can be combined.
items.action: Enable two or more compatible preferences and generate a plan.
items.expected: Every generated meal satisfies all selected preferences rather than only the last selection.

items.description: A grocery list is generated for missing ingredients.
items.action: Generate a plan that requires ingredients absent from or insufficiently stocked in the pantry.
items.expected: The grocery list includes every missing ingredient and the amount needed to cover the plan's deficit.

items.description: Fully available ingredients are excluded from the grocery list.
items.action: Generate a plan where one required ingredient is sufficiently stocked and another is missing.
items.expected: Only the missing or deficient amount is listed for purchase; the fully stocked ingredient is not.

items.description: Locking a meal preserves that meal during regeneration.
items.action: Lock one meal, record its recipe and quantities, and regenerate the plan with alternatives available.
items.expected: The locked meal and its ingredient amounts remain unchanged while unlocked meals are regenerated.

items.description: Locking a day preserves all meals on that day.
items.action: Lock one complete day, record its meals, and regenerate the rest of the plan.
items.expected: Every meal on the locked day remains unchanged while other unlocked days remain eligible for regeneration.

items.description: Unlocking restores eligibility for regeneration.
items.action: Unlock a previously locked meal or day and regenerate with an alternative available.
items.expected: The unlocked content is included in regeneration and is no longer guaranteed to retain its previous assignment.

items.description: Partial regeneration retains pantry and preference state.
items.action: Set pantry contents and preferences, lock part of a plan, and regenerate the remainder.
items.expected: The pantry entries, selected preferences, requested duration, and lock states remain in effect after regeneration.

items.description: The grocery list is recalculated after plan changes.
items.action: Record the grocery list, then regenerate unlocked meals so their ingredient needs differ.
items.expected: The grocery list updates to match the current plan and contains no obsolete missing-item amounts from the replaced meals.

items.description: Search competency models by job name.
items.action: Enter a job name that matches an available competency model and submit the search.
items.expected: The results list contains the matching job competency model.

items.description: Search competency models by competency-related keyword.
items.action: Enter a keyword present in an available model and submit the search.
items.expected: The results list contains each model matching that keyword and excludes unrelated models.

items.description: Open a competency model from search results.
items.action: Select one result from the competency-model results list.
items.expected: A detail view for the selected model opens and identifies the same job/model.

items.description: Present the competency model as a directed weighted graph.
items.action: Open a model containing multiple competencies and relationships.
items.expected: Competencies appear as distinguishable nodes, relationships show direction, and each relationship exposes its weight.

items.description: Keep graph content aligned with the selected model.
items.action: Open two different competency models in succession and compare their displayed graph content.
items.expected: The graph updates to the competencies and relationships of the currently selected model without retaining unrelated content from the previous model.

items.description: Adjust a competency level using drag and drop.
items.action: Drag an enabled competency's level control from its current value to another valid value and release it.
items.expected: The competency displays the new level immediately after the drop.

items.description: Modify a relationship weight.
items.action: Change an existing graph relationship to a different valid weight and commit the edit.
items.expected: The relationship displays and uses the new weight.

items.description: Temporarily disable and re-enable a competency.
items.action: Disable an enabled competency, then enable it again.
items.expected: The graph visibly reflects each state transition, and the competency returns to active participation when re-enabled.

items.description: Reject competency levels outside the supported range.
items.action: Attempt to assign a competency level below or above the limits communicated by the interface.
items.expected: The invalid level is not applied and clear validation feedback is shown.

items.description: Reject invalid relationship weights.
items.action: Attempt to save a nonnumeric or out-of-range relationship weight.
items.expected: The invalid weight is not applied and clear validation feedback identifies the problem.

items.description: Recalculate coverage after a competency-level change.
items.action: Record the displayed coverage, then change a level in a way that affects coverage.
items.expected: The displayed coverage recalculates immediately and reflects the changed level.

items.description: Recalculate critical paths after a relationship-weight change.
items.action: Record the displayed critical path, then modify a weight sufficiently to alter path criticality.
items.expected: The critical-path result updates immediately to reflect the new weight.

items.description: Recalculate risk gaps after disabling a competency.
items.action: Disable a competency whose absence creates or worsens a model gap.
items.expected: The risk-gap result updates immediately and identifies the resulting risk.

items.description: Raise and clear structural problem alerts dynamically.
items.action: Make a graph change that creates a reported problem, then reverse or correct that change.
items.expected: A relevant alert appears when the problem is introduced and clears or updates when the problem no longer exists.

items.description: Keep all derived analysis mutually consistent after sequential edits.
items.action: Change a competency level, a relationship weight, and an enabled state in sequence.
items.expected: After every edit, coverage, critical paths, risk gaps, and alerts all correspond to the latest graph state rather than an earlier state.

items.description: Build a model from the general template library.
items.action: Open the template library and choose an available general job competency template.
items.expected: A model is created or populated with the selected template's competencies and relationships.

items.description: Save a customized competency model as a template.
items.action: Modify a model, save it as a custom template with a valid distinct name, and return to the template library.
items.expected: The custom template appears in the library and retains the saved graph configuration when opened.

items.description: Require an identifiable custom template name.
items.action: Attempt to save a custom template with its name empty.
items.expected: The template is not saved and the interface requests a valid name.

items.description: Run recruitment, training, and promotion simulations.
items.action: Run the same model under each of the recruitment, training, and promotion scenarios.
items.expected: Each scenario produces a clearly labeled simulation result derived from the current model.

items.description: Refresh simulation results after model adjustments.
items.action: Run a scenario, change a relevant competency or relationship, and run or refresh that scenario again.
items.expected: The new simulation result reflects the adjusted model and does not present the previous result as current.

items.description: Browse the restaurant list.
items.action: Open the restaurant-browsing view.
items.expected: A list of available restaurants is displayed and each entry can be selected.

items.description: Open restaurant details.
items.action: Select a restaurant from the list.
items.expected: The selected restaurant's detail view opens.

items.description: Show required restaurant details.
items.action: Open a restaurant detail view.
items.expected: The view clearly identifies the restaurant and displays its cuisine type and average price.

items.description: Create a reservation with valid details.
items.action: Choose a future date, an offered time, and a valid party size, then complete the reservation.
items.expected: The reservation is created and a confirmation shows the selected restaurant, date, time, and party size.

items.description: Require all reservation scheduling fields.
items.action: Attempt to reserve while omitting the date, time, or party size one field at a time.
items.expected: No incomplete reservation is created and the missing field is identified.

items.description: Prevent reservation dates in the past.
items.action: Attempt to reserve a table for a past date.
items.expected: The reservation is rejected and clear date validation feedback is shown.

items.description: Reject invalid party sizes.
items.action: Attempt to reserve with zero, a negative value, a fractional value, or a value beyond any displayed limit.
items.expected: The reservation is not created and party-size validation feedback is shown.

items.description: Keep availability choices synchronized with reservation inputs.
items.action: Choose a date and time, then change the date or party size.
items.expected: The selectable time or availability state refreshes for the latest inputs without leaving an invalid stale selection active.

items.description: View upcoming reservations.
items.action: Create a future reservation and open the upcoming-bookings area.
items.expected: The new reservation appears with the correct restaurant, date, time, and party size.

items.description: Modify an upcoming reservation.
items.action: Open an upcoming booking, change at least one reservation field to another valid value, and save.
items.expected: The booking displays the new value and no duplicate booking is created.

items.description: Validate modified reservation details before applying them.
items.action: Enter an invalid date or party size while modifying an existing reservation and attempt to save.
items.expected: The modification is rejected, validation feedback is shown, and the previously valid booking remains unchanged.

items.description: Cancel an upcoming reservation.
items.action: Cancel an existing upcoming booking and confirm the cancellation if prompted.
items.expected: The booking is no longer presented as an active upcoming reservation and is clearly shown as canceled if retained in history.

items.description: Leave a reservation unchanged when cancellation is abandoned.
items.action: Start canceling a booking, then dismiss or decline the confirmation.
items.expected: The booking remains active with all original details.

items.description: Submit a review and rating for a visited restaurant.
items.action: For a restaurant with a completed visit, enter a valid rating and simple review and submit them.
items.expected: The review is accepted and displayed with the selected rating for the correct restaurant.

items.description: Restrict reviews to restaurants the user has visited.
items.action: Attempt to submit a review for a restaurant with no completed visit.
items.expected: The review is not accepted and the interface explains that only visited restaurants can be reviewed.

items.description: Reject ratings outside the displayed rating scale.
items.action: Attempt to submit a review with a rating below or above the allowed scale.
items.expected: The review is not submitted and rating validation feedback is shown.

items.description: Apply a valid discount coupon during reservation.
items.action: Enter a valid coupon in the reservation flow and apply it before completing the booking.
items.expected: The coupon is accepted and the displayed reservation price or discount summary reflects its benefit.

items.description: Handle invalid coupons without blocking an undiscounted reservation.
items.action: Enter an invalid coupon, attempt to apply it, then remove or ignore it and continue with valid reservation details.
items.expected: The invalid coupon gives clear feedback, no discount is applied, and the reservation can still be completed without a coupon.

items.description: Keep reservation totals and confirmation content consistent.
items.action: Complete a reservation after selecting its details and optionally applying a coupon.
items.expected: The final confirmation matches the selected booking details and any displayed discount or total from the checkout step.

items.description: Compare available software plans.
items.action: Open the plan comparison area.
items.expected: Multiple plans are displayed in a form that permits direct comparison.

items.description: Show detailed features for every plan.
items.action: Inspect each plan and open any available feature-detail view.
items.expected: Each plan has an identifiable name, price or billing terms, and a detailed description of included features.

items.description: Compare monthly, quarterly, and annual billing outcomes.
items.action: Switch the comparison among monthly, quarterly, and annual payment options.
items.expected: All three options produce clearly labeled, visibly updated pricing or billing outcomes for the plans.

items.description: Keep cadence pricing internally consistent.
items.action: For a plan, compare the displayed charge amount, billing frequency, and any stated effective-period total under all three cadences.
items.expected: The amounts and periods agree with each other and no cadence is mislabeled.

items.description: Prevent stale plan data when changing billing cadence.
items.action: Select one cadence, then rapidly switch to each other cadence.
items.expected: The selected cadence and every displayed price, total, and checkout choice consistently reflect the final selection.

items.description: Create a user account.
items.action: Enter valid values in the account-creation flow and submit.
items.expected: An account is created and the user can continue to subscription checkout.

items.description: Reject incomplete or invalid account submissions.
items.action: Submit the account form with each required field missing and with malformed input where a format is specified.
items.expected: The account is not created and clear field-specific validation is shown.

items.description: Subscribe through checkout.
items.action: Select a plan and billing cadence, create or use an account, provide valid checkout details, and confirm.
items.expected: The subscription is created for the exact selected plan and cadence and a clear confirmation is displayed.

items.description: Require valid checkout information.
items.action: Attempt to complete checkout with a required checkout field empty or invalid.
items.expected: No subscription is created and the invalid field is identified.

items.description: Keep checkout terms consistent with plan selection.
items.action: Select a plan and cadence, proceed to checkout, and compare the checkout summary with the comparison-page selection.
items.expected: Plan name, billing cadence, charge, and any stated totals or discounts match the selection.

items.description: Display the signed-in user's current plan.
items.action: Sign in as a subscribed user and open the account area.
items.expected: The account area identifies the user's active plan and billing cadence.

items.description: Display upcoming billing information.
items.action: Open billing information for an active subscription.
items.expected: The next billing date and expected charge or billing terms are clearly shown.

items.description: Protect subscription details from unsigned users.
items.action: While signed out, attempt to open the account subscription area.
items.expected: No user-specific subscription or billing information is exposed, and the user is prompted to sign in.

items.description: Change to a different subscription plan.
items.action: From an active subscription, choose a different plan, review its terms, and confirm the change.
items.expected: The account area reflects the newly selected plan and clearly communicates the applicable billing outcome.

items.description: Update upcoming billing after a plan or cadence change.
items.action: Change the current plan or payment cadence and return to upcoming billing information.
items.expected: The upcoming billing details update to the confirmed subscription terms without showing stale prior-plan information.

items.description: Preserve the current subscription when a plan change is abandoned.
items.action: Start changing plans, then cancel or navigate back before confirming.
items.expected: The original plan and its upcoming billing information remain unchanged.

items.description: Cancel an active subscription.
items.action: Choose subscription cancellation and confirm the action.
items.expected: The account clearly shows that the subscription is canceled or scheduled to end and communicates any remaining service period.

items.description: Preserve an active subscription when cancellation is declined.
items.action: Begin cancellation, then dismiss or decline the confirmation.
items.expected: The subscription remains active with the original plan and billing information.

items.description: Prevent repeated cancellation from producing conflicting state.
items.action: After confirming cancellation, attempt the cancellation action again if it remains available.
items.expected: The subscription remains in one unambiguous canceled state and no duplicate cancellation outcome is created.

items.description: Display submitted annotation tasks.
items.action: Open the annotation-review page.
items.expected: A list of submitted annotation tasks is displayed and each listed task can be opened.

items.description: Identify annotation tasks unambiguously.
items.action: Inspect the task list.
items.expected: Each task provides enough visible identifying information to distinguish it from the other tasks.

items.description: Open a task for review.
items.action: Select a task from the list.
items.expected: The selected task opens with its submitted annotations available for review.

items.description: Show annotations side-by-side with annotator attribution.
items.action: Open a task submitted by multiple annotators.
items.expected: The annotators' submissions are simultaneously visible in aligned side-by-side sections and each is attributed to the correct annotator.

items.description: Preserve annotation values exactly in the comparison.
items.action: Compare the annotation values in the task list/detail source with their side-by-side rendering.
items.expected: Labels, selections, or text are shown under the correct annotator without swapping, truncating essential content, or merging different submissions.

items.description: Approve an annotation task or review item.
items.action: Open an undecided task or item and mark it approved.
items.expected: Its review status changes to approved and remains visible when returning to the task list and reopening it.

items.description: Flag an annotation task or review item.
items.action: Open an undecided task or item and mark it flagged.
items.expected: Its review status changes to flagged and remains visible when returning to the task list and reopening it.

items.description: Keep approved and flagged states mutually unambiguous.
items.action: Mark an item approved and then mark the same item flagged, or perform the reverse transition.
items.expected: The item has one clear current review state, with the latest deliberate choice replacing or otherwise resolving the prior state.

items.description: Retain decisions while navigating between tasks.
items.action: Set a review status on one task, open a second task, then return to the first.
items.expected: The first task still displays the previously selected review status.

items.description: Open the annotation-quality summary.
items.action: Navigate to the summary view.
items.expected: The view shows disagreement statistics, the flagged-item count, and annotator inconsistency information.

items.description: Report disagreement rates accurately.
items.action: For a task or set with manually countable agreements and disagreements, calculate the rate and compare it with the summary.
items.expected: The displayed disagreement rate matches the underlying annotation comparisons and states its scope clearly.

items.description: Report the flagged-item count accurately.
items.action: Count currently flagged items and compare the count with the summary.
items.expected: The summary's flagged count equals the number of items currently marked flagged.

items.description: Identify the highest-inconsistency annotators accurately.
items.action: Derive each annotator's inconsistency rate from the available tasks and compare the highest value with the summary.
items.expected: The annotator or tied annotators with the highest derived rate are identified, with no lower-rate annotator presented as uniquely highest.

items.description: Update flagged statistics after a review decision changes.
items.action: Record the flagged count, flag one unflagged item, and reopen or refresh the summary.
items.expected: The flagged count increases by one and reflects the new review state.

items.description: Update flagged statistics when a flag is removed.
items.action: Change one flagged item to approved, then reopen or refresh the summary.
items.expected: The flagged count decreases by one and the item is no longer counted as flagged.

items.description: Avoid invalid statistics when no comparable annotations exist.
items.action: Open a task or summary scope with fewer than two comparable annotator submissions, if available.
items.expected: The interface shows an explicit unavailable or insufficient-data state rather than a misleading numeric disagreement rate.

items.description: Keep task-list and detail statuses synchronized.
items.action: Change a task's status in its detail view and return to the list.
items.expected: The corresponding list entry immediately displays the same current status.

items.description: Provide the three required batch-management tabs.
items.action: Open the laboratory sample-batch page.
items.expected: Tabs labeled Batch Table, Add/Edit, and Expiration Reminders are present and selectable.

items.description: Add a valid sample batch.
items.action: In Add/Edit, enter a distinct name, cabinet number, shelf number, and valid future expiration date, then save.
items.expected: The batch is created and appears in the Batch Table with all entered values.

items.description: Require all batch fields.
items.action: Attempt to save a new batch while omitting its name, cabinet number, shelf number, or expiration date one field at a time.
items.expected: No incomplete batch is saved and the missing field is clearly identified.

items.description: Reject an invalid expiration-date format.
items.action: Enter a date that does not follow the format communicated by the page and attempt to save.
items.expected: The batch is not saved and dedicated date-format feedback is displayed.

items.description: Reject a nonexistent calendar date.
items.action: Enter a correctly shaped but impossible date, such as a day that does not exist in its month, and attempt to save.
items.expected: The batch is not saved and the expiration date is identified as invalid.

items.description: Detect duplicate storage locations.
items.action: Create one batch, then attempt to save another batch using the same cabinet-and-shelf combination.
items.expected: The duplicate location is not silently accepted and dedicated duplicate-location feedback identifies the conflict.

items.description: Treat different shelves or cabinets as distinct locations.
items.action: After creating a batch, create another using the same cabinet with a different shelf, and another using the same shelf with a different cabinet.
items.expected: Both nonidentical cabinet-and-shelf combinations can be saved without duplicate-location feedback.

items.description: Display complete batch data in tabular form.
items.action: Open Batch Table after creating multiple batches.
items.expected: Each batch occupies a distinguishable table entry showing its name, cabinet, shelf, and expiration date under clear headings.

items.description: Load an existing batch for editing.
items.action: Choose an existing batch's edit action from the table.
items.expected: Add/Edit opens with that batch's current name, cabinet, shelf, and expiration date populated.

items.description: Edit batch information.
items.action: Change an existing batch's name, storage location, or expiration date to valid values and save.
items.expected: The existing batch is updated with the new values and no duplicate copy is created.

items.description: Apply duplicate-location validation during edits.
items.action: Edit one batch so that its cabinet-and-shelf combination matches another existing batch and attempt to save.
items.expected: The conflicting edit is rejected with dedicated duplicate-location feedback, and the previously saved location remains intact.

items.description: Synchronize newly added batches across tabs.
items.action: Save a new batch in Add/Edit and switch directly to Batch Table and Expiration Reminders.
items.expected: The new batch is immediately reflected in every applicable tab without a manual refresh.

items.description: Synchronize batch edits across tabs.
items.action: Edit a batch's name, location, or expiration date and inspect the other tabs.
items.expected: Every applicable tab immediately shows the updated values and no stale prior values.

items.description: Retain an in-progress Add/Edit form while switching tabs.
items.action: Enter a partial unsaved batch draft, switch to another tab, then return to Add/Edit.
items.expected: The draft values and editing context remain intact.

items.description: Retain the currently selected tab across a refresh.
items.action: Select a tab other than the initial tab and refresh the page.
items.expected: The page restores the same selected tab.

items.description: Retain an unsaved draft across a refresh.
items.action: Enter identifiable values in an unsaved Add/Edit form and refresh the page.
items.expected: The current draft and whether it represents an add or edit operation are restored without data loss.

items.description: Retain saved batch state during a lagged or interrupted refresh.
items.action: Create or edit a batch, simulate slow or unavailable network conditions, and refresh the page.
items.expected: The saved batch data reappears correctly and is not cleared or rolled back because of the network condition.

items.description: Show samples that are about to expire.
items.action: Create a batch expiring very soon, such as the next day, and open Expiration Reminders.
items.expected: The batch appears in the reminder view with its identifying information and expiration date.

items.description: Exclude clearly non-urgent batches from expiration reminders.
items.action: Create one batch expiring very soon and another expiring far in the future, then open Expiration Reminders.
items.expected: The soon-expiring batch is shown as needing attention while the far-future batch is not incorrectly shown as about to expire.

items.description: Recalculate reminders after an expiration-date edit.
items.action: Change a far-future batch to expire very soon and inspect Expiration Reminders, then change it back to a far-future date.
items.expected: The batch enters the reminder list after the first edit and leaves it after the second edit without requiring a page refresh.

items.description: Create more than one project.
items.action: Create a project named Alpha and another named Beta, then open the project list.
items.expected: Both Alpha and Beta appear as distinct selectable projects.

items.description: Keep each project's kanban tasks isolated.
items.action: Create a task named Alpha-only on Alpha's board, switch to Beta, and inspect Beta's board.
items.expected: Alpha-only is present on Alpha's board and absent from Beta's board.

items.description: Create a task with all requested planning attributes.
items.action: On a project board, create a task with a title, due date, priority, and assignee.
items.expected: The new task appears on the board with the entered due date, priority, and assignee.

items.description: Move a task between kanban columns by dragging it.
items.action: Drag an existing task card from its current column to a different column.
items.expected: The card is removed from the source column and appears in the destination column.

items.description: Persist a dragged task's new status.
items.action: After dragging a task to another column, reload the project page and locate the task.
items.expected: The task remains in the destination column after reload.

items.description: Filter tasks by status.
items.action: Create or identify tasks in different columns, apply a filter for one status, and inspect the visible cards.
items.expected: Only tasks with the selected status are shown.

items.description: Filter tasks by assignee.
items.action: Create or identify tasks assigned to different people, select one assignee filter, and inspect the visible cards.
items.expected: Every visible task is assigned to the selected person and other assignees' tasks are hidden.

items.description: Search tasks by keyword.
items.action: Enter a distinctive word from one task's title or content into the task search box.
items.expected: The matching task is shown and nonmatching tasks are hidden.

items.description: Clear task filtering and search state.
items.action: Apply a task filter and keyword search, then use the available clear or reset controls.
items.expected: The full project board task set is visible again.

items.description: Record progress on a task.
items.action: Open a task and change its progress from its initial value to a different available value, then save.
items.expected: The task displays the newly selected progress value.

items.description: Persist task progress updates.
items.action: Update a task's progress, reload the project page, and reopen the task.
items.expected: The updated progress value is retained after reload.

items.description: Show a concise overall project status summary.
items.action: Open a project containing tasks in at least two statuses and inspect its summary area.
items.expected: A compact summary reports the project's overall task status or progress rather than requiring every card to be opened.

items.description: Update the project summary when task status changes.
items.action: Note the summary, move a task to a different status, and inspect the summary again.
items.expected: The summary changes to reflect the task's new status.

items.description: Attach a discussion panel to each project.
items.action: Open a project and inspect its project workspace.
items.expected: A chat or discussion panel for that project is available from the workspace.

items.description: Send a project chat message.
items.action: Enter a unique message in a project's chat panel and submit it.
items.expected: The submitted message appears in that project's conversation.

items.description: Deliver new chat messages in real time.
items.action: Open the same project's chat in two team-member sessions and send a unique message from the first session without refreshing the second.
items.expected: The message appears in the second session without a manual page reload.

items.description: Keep project chats isolated.
items.action: Send a unique message in Alpha's chat, then open Beta's chat.
items.expected: The Alpha message remains in Alpha's chat and does not appear in Beta's chat.

items.description: Expose due date, priority, and assignee on task details.
items.action: Open a task created with a due date, priority, and assignee.
items.expected: All three saved attributes are visibly labeled or otherwise unambiguous.

items.description: Limit task search and filters to the active project.
items.action: Create similarly named tasks in two projects, open one project, and search or filter for the matching task.
items.expected: Results contain only tasks belonging to the active project.

items.description: Create a wedding planning dashboard with core details.
items.action: Enter a wedding date, budget, and guest count in a new planning dashboard and save it.
items.expected: The dashboard displays the saved wedding date, budget, and guest count.

items.description: Update wedding dashboard details.
items.action: Change the saved wedding date, budget, and guest count and save the update.
items.expected: The dashboard shows the new values instead of the previous values.

items.description: Persist wedding dashboard changes.
items.action: Save dashboard details, reload the page, and return to the dashboard.
items.expected: The most recently saved date, budget, and guest count remain visible.

items.description: Provide browsable venue listings.
items.action: Open the venue browsing area without entering a search term.
items.expected: Multiple venue listings are displayed with enough identifying information to distinguish them.

items.description: Provide browsable vendor listings.
items.action: Open the vendor browsing area without entering a search term.
items.expected: Multiple vendor listings are displayed with their service type or category identifiable.

items.description: Filter listings by location type.
items.action: Select one available location-type filter for applicable listings.
items.expected: Every visible result matches the selected location type.

items.description: Filter listings by price range.
items.action: Select one available price range in the venue or vendor listings.
items.expected: Every visible result falls within or is labeled with the selected price range.

items.description: Filter vendors by service type.
items.action: Select one vendor service type such as catering, photography, or another offered category.
items.expected: Every visible vendor result belongs to the selected service type.

items.description: Search venue and vendor listings by keyword.
items.action: Search using a distinctive venue or vendor name or listing keyword.
items.expected: Matching listings are returned and unrelated listings are excluded.

items.description: Reset listing filters and search.
items.action: Apply a listing filter and search term, then clear or reset them.
items.expected: The unfiltered listing collection is shown again.

items.description: Favorite a venue or vendor.
items.action: Mark an unfavorited listing as a favorite and open the favorites area.
items.expected: The selected listing is visibly favorited and appears in the favorites area.

items.description: Remove a venue or vendor from favorites.
items.action: Unfavorite a listing that is currently in the favorites area.
items.expected: The listing is no longer marked as a favorite and is removed from the favorites area.

items.description: Persist favorite listings for later retrieval.
items.action: Favorite a listing, reload or revisit the site, and open favorites.
items.expected: The favorited listing remains in the favorites area.

items.description: Offer a collection of planning tips.
items.action: Open the planning tips section and view an available tip.
items.expected: A collection of tips is available and the selected tip's useful planning content can be read.

items.description: Offer usable planning checklists.
items.action: Open the planning checklist section and inspect a checklist.
items.expected: The checklist presents distinct planning items that can be acted on or tracked.

items.description: Save a planning tip or checklist to the dashboard.
items.action: Choose an unsaved tip or checklist, save it, and return to the planning dashboard.
items.expected: The selected item appears in a saved planning section on the dashboard.

items.description: Mark a saved planning item as completed.
items.action: On the dashboard, mark one saved checklist item as completed.
items.expected: The item visibly changes to a completed state.

items.description: Persist planning-item completion state.
items.action: Mark a saved checklist item completed, reload the dashboard, and inspect that item.
items.expected: The item remains marked completed after reload.

items.description: Avoid duplicating the same saved planning resource.
items.action: Save the same tip or checklist to the dashboard twice.
items.expected: The dashboard contains one saved entry for that resource or clearly prevents the duplicate save.

items.description: Display a library of reusable text templates.
items.action: Open the template library and browse its available entries.
items.expected: Multiple selectable text templates are listed, including identifiable template types or categories.

items.description: Show template author and description.
items.action: Open a template's card or detail view.
items.expected: The template's author and description are both visible.

items.description: Select a template and expose its fill-in form.
items.action: Choose a template from the library.
items.expected: A simple form containing fields relevant to the selected template is displayed.

items.description: Generate a preview from entered form values.
items.action: Fill every required field in a selected template with distinctive valid values and request a preview.
items.expected: A preview is produced and includes the entered values in the template's intended structure.

items.description: Block generation when a required field is empty.
items.action: Leave one field marked required empty, complete the other fields, and attempt to generate or preview.
items.expected: Generation is prevented and the missing required field is clearly identified.

items.description: Reject restricted special characters in form input.
items.action: Enter disallowed formatting-sensitive special characters into a template input and attempt to generate.
items.expected: The invalid characters are rejected or validation blocks generation with a clear field-level message.

items.description: Submit a plain-text template.
items.action: Submit a new template in plain-text format with a unique title, author, description, category information, and body.
items.expected: The submission succeeds and the new template appears in the library.

items.description: Submit a Markdown template.
items.action: Submit a different new template in Markdown format with recognizable Markdown syntax and complete metadata.
items.expected: The submission succeeds and the Markdown template appears in the library with its content preserved or rendered correctly.

items.description: Retain submitted template metadata.
items.action: Open a newly submitted template from the library.
items.expected: Its displayed author, description, type or category, and body correspond to the submitted values.

items.description: Filter templates by template type.
items.action: Select one available template-type filter.
items.expected: Every visible result belongs to the selected template type.

items.description: Filter templates by applicable scenario.
items.action: Select one available applicable-scenario filter.
items.expected: Every visible result is associated with the selected scenario.

items.description: Filter or order templates by popularity.
items.action: Apply the available popularity criterion to the library.
items.expected: The visible results satisfy the selected popularity range or are ordered by popularity as indicated by the control.

items.description: Filter or order templates by update time.
items.action: Apply the available update-time criterion to the library.
items.expected: The visible results satisfy the selected update period or are ordered by update time as indicated by the control.

items.description: Combine multiple template search dimensions.
items.action: Apply a template type and an applicable scenario that have at least one known common result.
items.expected: Every visible result satisfies both selected criteria.

items.description: Fuzzy-match template keywords.
items.action: Search with a minor misspelling or partial variant of a known template keyword.
items.expected: The relevant template is returned despite the inexact keyword.

items.description: Show associative search suggestions in real time.
items.action: Type the first few characters of a known template title or keyword and pause without submitting the search.
items.expected: Relevant suggestions appear while typing, without requiring explicit search submission.

items.description: Use an associative suggestion to open or run a search.
items.action: Select one suggestion displayed beneath the template search box.
items.expected: The chosen suggestion populates or executes the search and shows the corresponding relevant result.

items.description: Add a template to favorites.
items.action: Favorite an unfavorited template and open the favorites list.
items.expected: The template is visibly favorited and appears in the favorites list.

items.description: Retrieve and use a template from favorites.
items.action: From the favorites list, select a saved template.
items.expected: The selected template opens with its details and fill-in form available.

items.description: Remove a template from favorites.
items.action: Unfavorite a template currently shown in the favorites list.
items.expected: The template loses its favorite state and no longer appears in the favorites list.

items.description: Create a detailed poll while signed in.
items.action: As a registered signed-in user, create a poll with a question, description, at least three choices, and a valid future deadline.
items.expected: The poll is created and displays the entered question, description, choices, and deadline.

items.description: Support polls without a voting deadline.
items.action: Create a second poll while leaving the optional deadline empty.
items.expected: The poll is created successfully and does not show an unintended deadline.

items.description: Require multiple choices when creating a poll.
items.action: Attempt to create a poll with only one voting choice.
items.expected: Creation is blocked and the user is prompted to provide multiple choices.

items.description: Create an anonymous-voting poll.
items.action: Create a poll with anonymous voting selected and open its share link in a signed-out session.
items.expected: The signed-out visitor can access the choices and submit a vote without signing in.

items.description: Enforce sign-in for a sign-in-required poll.
items.action: Create a poll that requires voters to sign in and open its share link in a signed-out session.
items.expected: Voting is blocked until the visitor signs in.

items.description: Provide a shareable poll link.
items.action: Use the creator's share control, copy the resulting link, and open it in another browser session.
items.expected: The link opens the intended poll rather than the dashboard or a different poll.

items.description: Submit a vote for one poll choice.
items.action: Open an active poll, select one choice, and submit the vote.
items.expected: The vote is accepted and a success state or results view is shown.

items.description: Show bar-style visual poll results.
items.action: View the results of a poll that has votes for at least two choices.
items.expected: Each choice has a bar-style visual breakdown with an understandable vote count, percentage, or equivalent magnitude.

items.description: Show live results to a voter immediately after voting.
items.action: Record the displayed results, cast a vote, and observe the results view without manually refreshing.
items.expected: The results become visible after submission and the selected choice's result increases accordingly.

items.description: Update results in another open session as votes arrive.
items.action: Keep the poll results open in one session and cast a vote from another session without refreshing the first.
items.expected: The first session's visual results update to include the new vote.

items.description: Close an active poll early.
items.action: As the poll creator, close an active poll before its deadline and revisit its voting page.
items.expected: The poll status is closed and new votes cannot be submitted.

items.description: Reopen a closed poll.
items.action: As the creator, reopen a previously closed poll and open its voting page.
items.expected: The poll returns to an active state and an eligible voter can submit a vote.

items.description: Switch a poll to read-only results mode.
items.action: As the creator, set an active poll to read-only results and open its public page.
items.expected: Results remain visible but voting controls are disabled or unavailable.

items.description: Prevent voting after the deadline.
items.action: Open a poll whose voting deadline has passed and attempt to vote.
items.expected: The poll indicates voting has ended and rejects the vote.

items.description: List the creator's polls on a dashboard.
items.action: Create multiple polls, including polls in different statuses, and open the creator dashboard.
items.expected: The user's polls are listed with enough title, creation-date, and status information to identify and manage them.

items.description: Search the poll dashboard by title.
items.action: Enter a distinctive substring from one owned poll's title into dashboard search.
items.expected: The matching poll is shown and nonmatching titled polls are excluded.

items.description: Sort dashboard polls by title.
items.action: Select title sorting and compare the order of at least three differently titled polls.
items.expected: Polls appear in the title order indicated by the sort control.

items.description: Sort dashboard polls by creation date.
items.action: Select creation-date sorting for polls created at different times.
items.expected: Polls appear in the chronological direction indicated by the sort control.

items.description: Sort dashboard polls by status.
items.action: Select status sorting while the dashboard contains polls with at least two statuses.
items.expected: Polls are grouped or ordered by status as indicated by the sort control.

items.description: Restrict poll management actions to the creator.
items.action: Open another user's poll while signed in as a non-creator and inspect or attempt its management controls.
items.expected: Close, reopen, and read-only management actions are unavailable or denied to the non-creator.
